subject: Cloud Computing
title: Twitch Source Code Leak
description: Learn Twitch Source Code Leak in one minute.

hook.text: In October 2021, Twitch's entire source code, internal tools, and streamer earnings were leaked online — 125 GB of data.

buildup.text: An attacker exploited a misconfigured server to access Twitch's internal Git repositories stored in the cloud.

discovery.text: The leak included source code, payment data for top streamers, and unreleased projects. Everything became public.

twist.text: Twitch's parent company is Amazon — the company that runs AWS. Even Amazon's own subsidiary was misconfigured.

climax.text: The breach showed that source code is a high-value target. Protecting repositories is as critical as protecting data.

punchline.text: Amazon's own subsidiary leaked everything. Cloud security spares nobody.

quiz.question: What made the Twitch breach especially ironic?
options: Twitch is owned by Amazon, which operates AWS
The leaked data was already publicly available
The breach was intentionally planned by Twitch's marketing team

details.summary: In 2021, an anonymous user leaked 125 GB of Twitch internal data including source code, creator payment data, and internal tools. The breach was attributed to a server misconfiguration that allowed unauthorized access to Twitch's version control systems.
details.whyItMatters: The Twitch leak demonstrated that intellectual property and internal data face the same cloud misconfiguration risks as customer data. Source code exposure enables further attacks.
takeaways: 125 GB of source code and internal data were leaked
Creator payment information was publicly exposed
A server misconfiguration enabled the unauthorized access

faq.question: What was included in the Twitch leak?
faq.answer: The full Twitch source code, creator payout data since 2019, internal security tools, an unreleased Steam competitor called Vapor, and company documentation were all included. The anonymous leaker posted everything to a public torrent.

faq.question: How can source code leaks be prevented?
faq.answer: Restrict access to version control systems, enforce network segmentation, monitor for unusual data access volumes, require MFA for developer tools, audit server configurations regularly, and implement data loss prevention that detects large-scale data transfers.
